newsitem.title: USA: Prospects for US/EU meat agreement not good - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Prospects for US/EU meat agreement not good - USDA.

text.p: A senior Agriculture Department official said Thursday that U.S. officials are very pessimistic about the chances for an agreement with the European Union on meat and poultry inspection rules.
"Right now, there is a high degree of pessimism based on the apparent lack of flexibility demonstrated by the Europeans," said the official, who did not want to be identified.
The official said the USDA would make a counter offer to Thursday night in response to EU proposals put forward this week and that the two sides will meet again on Friday.
But U.S. industry representatives also said it would take a minor miracle for negotiators to reach an agreement in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks by an approaching April 1 deadline.
"These guys are not negotiating in good faith," said Nick Girodano of the National Pork Producers Council. "The EU just doesn't want our red meat in their market."

Negotiators have been meeting in Washington all week to resolve the years-old dispute which could threaten several hundreds of millions of dollars worth of trade in meat, poultry, dairy, eggs and pet food.

Agriculture Department officials held separate briefings with the meat, poultry and dairy sectors throughout the day Thursday to get their input, and sources said that "the meat and poultry people were not happy."
